rows.observation: Excavator was engulfed by rocks from a highwall failure while operating at the base of the face.
Miner sustained fatal electrical injuries during routine maintenance of underground power distribution system.
Contractor was engulfed while entering a confined space vessel without following entry permit procedures.
Haul truck flipped over after driving off a haulage ramp edge due to lack of berms.
Highwall face collapse trapped operator during overburden removal.
Worker inhaled high concentration of dust during dry sweeping operation.
Worker struck by 200lb tire rolling from improperly blocked stockpile area.
Worker reached into rotating conveyor pulley and was entangled.
Haul truck rolled over embankment due to missing berm at roadway edge.
Electrical fire in substation due to improper cable insulation maintenance.
Worker entangled in rotating conveyor pulley guard during machine run.
Haul truck crashed at intersection due to failing to yield in high-traffic pit area.
Maintenance worker bypassed lockout during equipment repair.
Substation fire due to short circuit, no suppression used.
Electrician caught by energized drill motor after bypass of safety interlock.
Equipment maintenance on unblocked drive system led to crush.
Operator trapped after highwall bench collapsed during scaling.
Emergency exit was blocked by production pallets and illuminated signage was not visible.
Forklift operator struck a worker while exceeding the speed limit and driving blind at an aisle corner.
Electrician was working near energized equipment without appropriate arc flash clothing or training.
Crane boom contacted overhead energized power lines during load positioning.
Overhead crane load dropped when lifting cable frayed severely; no inspection conducted.
Forklift sped through blind aisle without using horn, nearly striking worker.
7-foot deep trench excavation lacking required shoring system and means of egress.
Worker suffered respiratory damage from ammonia vapor exposure due to ventilation system failure.
Emergency fire exit aisle completely blocked by stacked pallets.
Worker fell from ladder without securing top rails.
Ammonia vapor exposure after ventilation system shutdown for maintenance without supplemental PFD/resp-prot.
Amputation from unguarded conveyor drive point.
Excavation crew in 7ft trench without shoring or trench box protection.
Worker suffered respiratory distress after ammonia exposure when local exhaust failed.
Live wiring exposed in terminal box due to missing junction cover.
Emergency fire exit was blocked by stacked shelving and materials.
Multiple chemical drums labeled improperly in production prep zone.
Corrosive vapor leak occurred; area lacked emergency ventilation and spill cleanup gear.
Forklift sped through blind aisle without using horn.
No fall harness while installing roof deck at 25 feet.
Lab worker not trained on handling chemical agents, leading to improper storage label violation.
A closed electrical panel was present in the hallway, but no exposed parts, damage, heat, smoke, or open cover were observed. The actual issue was boxes stored in the walking path.

A contractor repair shop near the quarry had an unguarded bench grinder. The note does not confirm whether the shop is on mine property, whether miners use it, or whether OSHA or MSHA jurisdiction applies.
A haul truck backed toward the stockpile dump edge. The berm looked low in the photo, but the image does not show berm height, tire size, dump-point condition, or whether a spotter was present.

A trailing cable was hanging low across the rib line near a travelway. The jacket appeared intact, but miners and mobile equipment pass through the area. The note does not confirm whether the cable was energized or protected from damage.
A mechanic was repairing a pump outside during freezing rain. The report says gloves were wet, but does not document exposure duration, warming breaks, dry PPE, wind chill, or supervisor monitoring.

During a plant walkdown, the inspector noted a belt conveyor area where a roller could be reached from the walkway. The note says guarding may be incomplete, but the photo angle does not clearly show whether a fixed guard is installed.

A refuge chamber route marker was missing at an intersection, but the travelway itself was open and clear. The observation does not confirm whether alternate route markers were visible or whether miners had current evacuation maps.

A plant conveyor tail pulley had a damaged guard, and water was pooling near a motor junction box. Employees walk through the area to adjust material flow. The note does not confirm whether the junction box was energized or whether the conveyor was locked out.

Loose rock was visible on the highwall above the pit road. A haul truck route passed below the area. The note does not confirm whether the road was closed, bermed off, scaled, or examined by a competent person.
Water was running across the floor in front of an open electrical panel, and employees were walking through the area to reach the time clock. The note does not confirm whether parts were energized.
A welder was working from a scaffold near stored cardboard. The note does not confirm scaffold guardrails, fire watch, combustible clearance, or whether fall protection was required.
A mobile crane was operating near a laydown area. Workers were walking near the counterweight side, and the swing radius barricade was not visible in the photo.

A worker was near the edge of a low-slope roof unloading material. The note does not show distance to the edge, roof height, warning line status, guardrail, safety monitor, or personal fall arrest setup.

Several vertical rebar ends were exposed near a construction walking path. Employees were carrying material through the area, but the note does not identify whether caps or impalement protection were available nearby.

Oxygen and acetylene cylinders were stored side by side near the welding cart. They were not separated by distance or a fire-rated barrier, and the note does not confirm valve caps, securement, or whether cylinders were in use.
An electrical panel was located in the office hallway. The panel door was fully closed, latched, undamaged, and there were no exposed wires, sparks, heat, or moisture present.

A qualified electrical technician was performing voltage testing on an open, energized motor control center. The technician was wearing certified Category 4 arc flash PPE and using insulated probes under a hot work permit.

A pallet of supplies was stored directly in front of the emergency eyewash next to corrosive cleaner containers. The note does not confirm whether the eyewash was functional, inspected, or reachable within the required time.
In the warehouse shipping department, the pedestrian egress ramp was blocked by stacked wooden pallets, preventing emergency evacuation access. No excavation or construction work was present.
Forklift batteries were being charged in the maintenance bay. The eyewash station was not visible and the note does not confirm ventilation, acid spill supplies, or emergency eyewash access.
Boxes were stacked in front of an electrical panel. The panel door was closed and there was no exposed wiring. The issue appears to be access and clearance, not exposed live parts.

Hot work was occurring in the maintenance shop. The permit was posted, nearby combustibles were cleared, an extinguisher was present, and a fire watch was assigned. The note asks whether additional evidence is needed before closing.
Boxes of metal parts were stacked unevenly on a storage rack beside an employee walkway. Some boxes leaned over the rack edge, but no forklift movement or suspended load was involved.

Employees wore dust masks voluntarily while sweeping packaging dust. The note does not confirm contaminant type, airborne measurements, required respirator program elements, or whether the masks were required by management.

Employee was handling cut sheet metal with sharp edges and no gloves were visible. The note does not mention whether cut-resistant gloves were available, whether other handling tools were used, or whether an injury occurred.
No welding, cutting, brazing, or grinding was occurring. Oily rags and cardboard were piled next to a portable heater in the maintenance room.
Unlabeled solvent bottles were stored on the floor beside cardboard waste, and the containers partially blocked the aisle. No hot work was occurring and no spill was visible.

A worker was dry cutting concrete block inside a renovation area and visible dust was drifting toward another employee. The note does not mention water delivery, vacuum collection, respiratory protection, or exposure assessment.
Employees were observed laying pipe inside a 5-foot deep trench excavation. No stairway, ladder, ramp, or other safe means of egress was visible or provided inside the trench.
The inspector uploaded a blurry photo and wrote only 'unsafe?' No task, location, equipment, employee exposure, or condition details were provided.
